answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to build a costly, verifiable history before it can vote or claim rewards. A new identity starts with no trust and must complete small, checked tasks, with stake locked and slashed if it misbehaves. Like a sparrow crossing a canyon, a fake identity cannot simply appear on the other side; it must make the whole journey. If an attacker spawns many identities, the cost spirals upward, since each needs its own stake, time, and successful work. This makes mass fakery expensive and slow, without blocking genuine newcomers.
